summary: Facepalm: Facepalm scan for 2026-10-05. I'm submitting no candidates. The search tool hit its usage limit before I could open two accepted sources for any story that was in the window. The closest lead was the Calaveras County, Calif., voter-pamphlet printing error, announced Sunday, Oct. 4. Its only accepted-publisher page is an ABC10 video page that couldn't be fetched, and the other coverage is on non-accepted outlets or Yahoo. Every other lead was either outside the window or had no accepted sources. Genius: Scan for 2026-10-05 (GENIUS). I found one solid candidate: Stanford's Karl Deisseroth shares the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for optogenetics. It was announced Oct. 5, within the window, and I opened STAT and Nature, both dated Oct. 5. The physics and chemistry Nobels fall after the scan date. The server's search limit was hit early, so I could not finish checking any alternates. Those leads are listed under passed. No facepalm story met the standard; nothing published. The verified genius story is on the bench for a later day.

candidates.headline: Stanford's Karl Deisseroth shares the 2026 Nobel Prize in medicine for optogenetics
candidates.reason: passed every check; kept for a later day because the other side had no story

candidates.headline: Calaveras County, Calif., voter pamphlets mailed with June primary candidate statements instead of November ones
candidates.reason: In the date window (the county announced it Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026). The only accepted-publisher page found was an ABC10 video page, which couldn't be fetched. The other coverage is on outlets not on the accepted list (Union Democrat, FOX40, myMotherLode, Calaveras Enterprise) or on Yahoo. Search capacity ran out before a second accepted source turned up.

candidates.headline: Hagerstown, Md., fixes 'Municpal Stadium' sign after 20 years
candidates.reason: The Tucson.com page republishes an old AP story (the city's population is given as 38,000, and it says the sign went up in the 1980s and stood for 20 years), so this isn't a recent event. I also couldn't open the page.

candidates.headline: UnitedHealthcare letters wrongly tell members eight clinicians had died
candidates.reason: First reported Oct. 7–8, 2026 (Star Tribune, Becker's), after the scan date. The letters themselves are dated Sept. 11, which is also outside the 7-day window.

candidates.headline: GOP ad misidentifies Democrat Jonathan Nez as Republican Myron Lizer
candidates.reason: Reported Oct. 9, 2026, after the scan date. The subject is also Republican, and that party isn't currently allowed.

candidates.headline: Mono County, Calif., mails corrected voter information guides after printing error
candidates.reason: Appears to have been reported around Oct. 6–7, 2026, after the scan date. The only source found (Eastern Sierra Now) isn't on the accepted list.

candidates.headline: Bradford County, Pa., mail-in ballots delayed by printing vendor
candidates.reason: The only coverage found was The Daily Review, which isn't on the accepted list. A delay isn't clearly a self-evident blunder either.

candidates.headline: Thurston County, Wash., handcuffed suspect escapes patrol car
candidates.reason: Reported around Oct. 7, 2026, after the scan date. The coverage found (MyNorthwest, Yahoo) isn't accepted, and the subject is a criminal suspect, not an institutional blunder.

candidates.headline: Fervo Energy's Cape Station in Utah reaches commercial operation as the first enhanced geothermal plant (Oct. 1)
candidates.reason: The only accepted source found was TechCrunch (Oct. 1). Every other page was a press-release wire, Yahoo, or a site that is not accepted. The search limit was reached before a second accepted publisher could be found. It is also partly a company milestone.

candidates.headline: JILA/NIST physicist Jun Ye (Boulder, CO) named a 2026 Wolf Prize in Physics laureate
candidates.reason: The only coverage found was from the university, NIST and the Wolf Foundation, plus JPost and JNS, which are not accepted. No accepted news publisher was found.

candidates.headline: Stanford scientists turn a cancer driver into a 'kill switch' (ScienceDaily, Oct. 5)
candidates.reason: Seen only as a ScienceDaily headline. The publication date and a second accepted source were not checked before the search limit was reached.

candidates.headline: Nobel Prize in physics to Francis Halzen; Wolf Prize medicine and chemistry laureates
candidates.reason: The physics Nobel was announced Oct. 6, after the scan date. US-based Wolf laureates in other fields were not identified or sourced.
